title: React State
summary: How components remember data and update their interfaces.
explanation: State is information a React component remembers between renders. When its state changes, React can render the component again with the new value.
bubbleAnalogy: A Bubble custom state stores temporary data on an element; workflows can update it and conditional expressions can respond. React's useState fills a similar role for interactive component data. It's a conceptual analogy, not an identical implementation.
insight: Changing an ordinary variable doesn't notify React that an interface needs updating. React state changes trigger the rendering process.
appliedIn: Planned for NextHop's Discover filters. Not implemented yet.
checkQuestions: When should I use state instead of a regular variable?
What is the difference between props and state?
When should state move into a parent component?

title: React Components
summary: Building reusable interface pieces with clearly defined inputs.
explanation: A component is a function that returns user interface elements. You can reuse it throughout a project and pass information into it using props.
bubbleAnalogy: Bubble's reusable elements and React components reduce repeated UI work. React props are similar in purpose to properties exposed by a reusable element.
insight: A component should have a clear responsibility. It doesn't need to be reusable everywhere to be useful.
appliedIn: Planned for NextHop's camp cards. Not implemented yet.
checkQuestions: Why split a screen into components?
How can two components share data?

title: Row Level Security
summary: Enforcing per-user data permissions inside a database.
explanation: Row Level Security (RLS) lets PostgreSQL apply policies controlling which database records a request may read or change.
bubbleAnalogy: Bubble Privacy Rules are a helpful comparison. Both express access restrictions on data, rather than relying on hidden buttons or pages to protect private information.
insight: Authentication proves who a user is. Authorization decides which resources that user can access.
appliedIn: Planned for NextHop wishlists. Not implemented yet.
checkQuestions: Why doesn't hiding a button secure data?
How would I test access with two accounts?
What is the difference between auth and RLS?

title: Git vs. GitHub
summary: Local version control and remote repository hosting.
explanation: Git is a version-control system on your machine. GitHub is a service that hosts Git repositories and supports code review and collaboration.
bubbleAnalogy: Bubble has development/live versions and history. Git also tracks changes over time, but at the level of files and commits in a repository.
codeExample:
git status
git add .
git commit -m "Build notebook search"
git push
insight: A commit should describe a small, meaningful change. Before committing agent-generated code, inspect the diff.
appliedIn: Planned for the first Developer Notebook repository commit.
checkQuestions: How is a push different from a commit?
When would I create a branch?

title: TypeScript Types
summary: Defining data shapes so the editor catches mistakes earlier.
explanation: TypeScript describes expected data types and checks code before it runs. These checks help developers discover certain mistakes early.
bubbleAnalogy: Bubble fields have types, and option sets constrain expected choices. TypeScript can describe similar expectations in code, but types aren't a database schema or runtime input validation.
insight: Types improve developer feedback, but an API response can still contain unexpected values. Runtime validation may also be necessary.
appliedIn: This notebook uses KnowledgeEntry and JournalEntry TypeScript types.
checkQuestions: What does an optional property mean?
Can TypeScript secure data received from an API?

title: Next.js App Router
summary: Organizing pages, layouts and server/client behavior.
explanation: Next.js builds on React. With the App Router, folders and special files establish routes and layouts. Components can render on the server or run interactively in the browser.
bubbleAnalogy: A Next.js route resembles a Bubble page URL in purpose. Server-side code has some similarities to Bubble backend workflows, but is executed and deployed differently.
codeExample:
src/app/
  page.tsx
  layout.tsx
  camps/
    page.tsx
    [slug]/
      page.tsx
insight: Never put secret API keys in code that gets sent to the browser.
appliedIn: The Developer Notebook home route is implemented at src/app/page.tsx.
checkQuestions: What determines the home page URL?
Which parts of an app need client-side JavaScript?

title: Designing the Developer Notebook
summary: Agreed on a small searchable learning library that visually extends the existing portfolio.
objective: Choose a useful note-taking structure and a visual direction before writing the first application code.
decisions: Use a desktop-first dark interface with warm beige accents. Center the MVP on Knowledge Entries and Build Journal. Include Bubble analogies in technical explanations. Use Next.js and TypeScript.
aiAssistance: Used ChatGPT to discuss the product scope and build a clickable design preview.
challenges: Avoiding a generic dashboard design and keeping the scope small enough to learn alongside NextHop.
verification: Reviewed and approved an interactive design concept. Production code, persistence, authentication and deployment were not yet completed during this planning session.
lessons: A clear content model and a well-defined MVP are more useful at this stage than adding advanced features.
next: Set up the Next.js project, inspect its architecture, and run it locally.
